hindi_name: टमाटर का अगेती अंगमारी / झुलसा रोग
favorable_conditions: Warm temperature (24-29°C), humidity >80%, older plant tissue, stressed or overcrowded plants, heavy dew
economic_impact: 30-50% yield loss in uncontrolled epidemics. Most common foliar disease of tomato in India.
symptoms: Dark brown to black concentric ring spots (target-board pattern) on lower leaves first
Spots are oval/angular, 0.5-1.5 cm diameter, with yellow halo
Lower leaves yellow and drop prematurely (defoliation from bottom up)
Collar rot: dark sunken lesion on stem near soil line (seedling stage)
Fruit rot: dark leathery sunken spots at stem-end of fruit

treatment.chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP (Dithane M-45) at 2.5g/L water, starting from 30 days after transplanting. Alternate with Chlorothalonil 75% WP at 2g/L. For severe infection, use Azoxystrobin 23% SC (Amistar) at 1ml/L.
treatment.biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride at 4g/kg seed. Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens at 5g/L.
treatment.cultural: Remove and destroy lower infected leaves. Mulch with straw to prevent soil splash. Maintain proper spacing (60×45 cm). Avoid overhead irrigation. Stake plants.
treatment.dosage: 2.5g per liter of water, 500g per acre

source: ICAR-IIHR Bangalore; PAU Ludhiana Vegetable Advisory

favorable_conditions: Cool nights (12-18°C), warm days (15-25°C), heavy rain/fog, relative humidity >90%, cloudy weather for 2+ consecutive days
economic_impact: 70-100% crop loss possible within 1-2 weeks if untreated. Can devastate entire fields. Shares same pathogen as Irish Potato Famine.
symptoms: Water-soaked, dark green to brown lesions on leaf tips and margins
White cottony fungal growth (sporangia) on underside of leaves during humidity
Lesions rapidly enlarge and turn black — entire leaf collapses
Stems show dark brown/black lesions with white growth
Fruit develops greasy brown-grey firm rot, often on upper half

treatment.chemical: EMERGENCY spray Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Curzate M-8) at 3g/L water immediately upon detection. Alternate with Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold MZ) at 2.5g/L. Spray every 5-7 days during epidemic conditions.
treatment.biological: Preventive application of Trichoderma harzianum at soil drenching. Neem-based formulations as supplementary.
treatment.cultural: Remove and burn ALL infected plant material. Do NOT compost. Avoid planting near potato fields. Ensure proper drainage. Avoid overhead watering.
treatment.dosage: 3g per liter of water, emergency spray

source: ICAR-IIHR; Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) Shimla

hindi_name: टमाटर के पत्ते का फफूंद रोग
favorable_conditions: High humidity (>85%), temperature 20-25°C, poor ventilation in polyhouses/greenhouses, dense canopy
economic_impact: 20-50% yield loss in greenhouse tomatoes. Primarily a greenhouse/polyhouse disease.
symptoms: Pale green to yellowish diffuse spots on upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety fungal growth on lower leaf surface (key diagnostic)
Infected leaves curl upward and wilt
Severe infection causes premature defoliation
May also infect stems and pedicels in high humidity

treatment.chemical: Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP (Kavach) at 2g/L water. For resistant strains, use Azoxystrobin 23% SC at 1ml/L.
treatment.biological: Apply Bacillus subtilis formulation as preventive spray at 5g/L.
treatment.cultural: Improve greenhouse ventilation — open side panels during day. Reduce humidity below 80%. Remove lower leaves for airflow. Drip irrigation only.

resistant_varieties: Hybrid varieties with Cf resistance genes

hindi_name: टमाटर का सेप्टोरिया पत्ती धब्बा रोग
favorable_conditions: Warm temperature (20-25°C), prolonged wet weather, rain splash, overhead irrigation, poor sanitation
economic_impact: 10-40% yield loss due to early defoliation. Reduces fruit quality and sunscald.
symptoms: Numerous small (2-3 mm) circular spots with dark brown border and grey/tan center
Tiny black dots (pycnidia) visible in center of spots with hand lens — key diagnostic
Lower and middle leaves affected first, progressing upward
Heavy infection causes leaves to yellow, dry, and fall off
Fruit rarely affected, but exposed fruit gets sunscald from defoliation

treatment.chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5g/L water or Chlorothalonil 75% WP at 2g/L. Begin at first sign and repeat every 10-14 days. Add a sticker for better coverage.
treatment.biological: Apply copper-based organic fungicides (Bordeaux mixture 1%). Neem oil spray at 5ml/L as supplementary.
treatment.cultural: Remove infected lower leaves. Mulch to prevent rain splash. 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops. Destroy all crop debris after harvest.

resistant_varieties: No fully resistant commercial variety; Arka Vikas shows tolerance

scientific_name: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV, family Geminiviridae)
hindi_name: टमाटर का पीला पत्ती मोड़ विषाणु रोग
favorable_conditions: High whitefly populations, warm dry weather (25-35°C), nearby alternate hosts, year-round tomato cropping
economic_impact: 80-100% yield loss if infection occurs before flowering. The most devastating viral disease of tomato in India and globally.
symptoms: Severe upward and inward curling of leaflets — cupping shape
Leaves become small, crinkled, and bright yellow at margins
Stunted plant growth — internodes shortened
Flower drop — severely infected plants produce no fruit
Plants infected early become bushy with no harvestable yield

treatment.chemical: No cure for virus. Control whitefly vector: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (Confidor) at 0.3ml/L water. Alternate with Thiamethoxam 25% WG (Actara) at 0.3g/L. Spray undersides of leaves.
treatment.biological: Install yellow sticky traps (12-15 per acre). Spray neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.15%) at 3ml/L. Release Encarsia formosa parasitoids in greenhouses.
treatment.cultural: Remove and burn infected plants immediately. Use 40-mesh nylon net screens. Avoid planting near old infected fields. Grow barrier crops (maize, sorghum) around tomato.

source: ICAR-IIHR Bangalore; Asian Vegetable Research and Development Center (AVRDC)
